subject: Identity cutover playbook: SCIM-proofing & service-account ops

From: Maria Perez <maria.perez@orchidsys.com>

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production cutover: SSO / SCIM / IP allowlist coordination

Hi Tessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re targeting a production cutover for Orchid Systems the week of June 14 and I wanted to get alignment on the access controls workstream. High level asks from my side:

- Confirm SSO (SAML) metadata exchange and test accounts window
- SCIM provisioning schedule and expected user attribute mapping (we currently use employeeId and externalId)
- Static IP allowlist ranges for the cutover and any maintenance windows where IPs might change
- Service account requirements (scopes/least-privilege) used by our provisioning jobs

If you can share a runbook and owners we can lock the date. We’ll also need the SOC2 evidence checklist for changes that touch identity. I’ve attached our SAML metadata and the security contact alias.

Attachments: orchid-saml-metadata.xml (xml)

Regards,
Maria Perez
Director, IT Operations — Orchid Systems
security-ops@orchidsys.com

Hi Maria —

Appreciate the timeline. Draft plan below and attached is the first-cut cutover runbook (redwood-orchard-cutover-runbook-v0.9.pdf). Key points:

1) Pre-cutover (Week of June 7)
   - Exchange SAML metadata and verify cert validity (owner: Orchid SecOps)
   - Create 2 test SSO accounts (IdP-provisioned) to validate role mappings
   - SCIM staging sync: run a full delta sync and snapshot user attributes for reconciliation

2) Dry-run (June 10)
   - Dry-run in staging during off-hours (2 hour window). Redwood will capture logs and token traces.

3) Cutover (June 14, 00:00–02:00 local)
   - IP allowlist: Redwood production egress will come from these ranges: 34.210.112.0/24, 52.44.18.0/24 (please confirm acceptance)
   - Service accounts: we recommend a single provisioning service account scoped to SCIM write + read, no user mgmt console access. See section 3.2 of runbook for least-privilege policy.
   - Rollback plan: revert to IdP-only test group and disable SCIM sync.

4) Post-cutover (June 14–16)
   - Reconciliation report, user count, failures, and regression alerts.

Action items for Orchid: share any additional IP ranges you require, confirm SAML cert expiration, and nominate the IdP admin who will approve test users.

I’ve linked a JIRA for the work: JIRA-OPS-7821 — we’ll attach runbook updates there. Monica — can you confirm the runbook sections for service-account creation and the recommended IAM policy? Ben — can you own the dry-run?

Attachments: redwood-orchard-cutover-runbook-v0.9.pdf

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
<tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Direct: +1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Tessa — this looks good. Quick responses below:

- IP ranges: we can accept 34.210.112.0/24 and 52.44.18.0/24. Our egress NATs are 18.204.0.0/16 for fallback; we need confirmation that fallback won’t be used during the cutover window (we can coordinate firewall rules).
- SAML cert: expires 2028-01-10 — fine for now.
- IdP admin: I’ll assign Chris Lang (chris.lang@orchidsys.com) to approve test accounts.
- SCIM attributes: we will expose employeeId and externalId. Our provisioning jobs run every 15 minutes and need a service account that can PATCH users and read groups. Least-privilege sounds right; do you have a sample policy?

I’ve attached the Orcid SAML metadata and a short network diagram.

Attachments: orchid-saml-metadata.xml (attached)

—
Maria Perez
Director, IT Operations — Orchid Systems

- [Tessa] Confirm cutover approval and change window with Orchid (I’ll prepare the change request template).

- Create a shared Slack channel with Orchid SecOps (proposed: #orchid-cutover) and add Chris Lang + security-ops@orchidsys.com.

Ben — can you take the dry-run on June 10 (22:00–00:00 PDT)? I’ll prepare the test cases and failure injection scenarios (SCIM partial failures, SAML redirect latency).

Thanks — will update the JIRA and attach the finalized runbook after the DR.
